message.content: This file implements the Unix `cat` command, a utility that concatenates and displays the contents of one or more files to standard output. It supports several command-line options including `-n` (line numbers), `-b` (line numbers skipping blanks), `-u` (unbuffered output), `-e` (show end-of-line markers), `-t` (show tabs), and `-v` (show non-printing characters). The program parses flags in a loop, validates that input files are not the same as the output file, then either processes characters one at a time via `copyopt()` or uses bulk I/O via `fastcat()`. Key exported functions include `main()` which orchestrates file selection and option handling, `copyopt()` which formats and outputs characters with optional line numbering and special character display, and `fastcat()` which performs optimized block-level reading and writing using `read()` and `write()` system calls. The code depends on standard C libraries (`stdio.h`, `unistd.h`, `sys/stat.h`, etc.) and relies on `BUFSIZ` (the kernel block size) for its buffer allocation. Notable design decisions include the use of a `struct cat_state` to track formatting options and line numbers, the `CAT_IN_LINE` flag to avoid redundant line numbers within a single line, and the `fastcat()` function which drains full blocks from a pipe to avoid partial reads.

- Detects if input is the same file as output to prevent self-reading
- Uses `getc()`/`putc()` for character-level processing in `copyopt()`
- Uses `read()`/`write()` in `fastcat()` for bulk I/O
